newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch railways faces three new freight competitors.
newsitem.headline: Dutch railways faces three new freight competitors.

text.p: Dutch state-owned rail company Nederlandse Spoorwegen (NS) faces the prospect of three new rivals to its freight unit NS Cargo by the end of the year, Dutch media reported on Saturday.
The would-be competitors offer the first challenge to NS Cargo's domination of rail cargo transport in the Netherlands.

The three are a conglomerate of waste transporters, Rotterdam-based Short Lines and German firm Bentheimer Eisenbahn. All believe they will be able to undercut NS's prices for bulk goods and container transport and, at least initially, all would operate on NS's existing rail network.
ACTS, the grouping of three waste transporters, proposes establishing a service to carry waste from the urban heartland to the north of the Netherlands.
Short Lines would run from Rotterdam to northern and eastern parts of the country.
Bentheimer Eisenbahn's proposal offers a three times daily link from Coevorden on the German border to Rotterdam and would be an extension of its current line in Germany.

Dutch railways already faces one competitor in its passenger operations, Lovers Rail. Lovers currently has only a handful of services, but competition seems set to rise after CGEA, a unit of France's Compagnie Generale des Eaux took a 70 percent stake in the company earlier this month.
